content:
- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or trending negative — model ignores downward momentum.
- Model overreacts to recent price spikes; true price often corrects within 3–5 days after a forecast peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds high forecasts for too long after a sharp rise; true price often pulls back toward prior 10–15 day average.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic in bullish sentiment periods — true price often declines after initial surge.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model fails to smooth transitions — forecasts jump between extremes without proper decay.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after strong bullish sentiment — especially when sentiment drops below 0.30.
- Forecast should adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.25 and price has been rising for 5+ days — true price often reverses within 7 days.
